title: Adic coefficient datum and reduction tower
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and use its small pro-etale site, constant coefficient sheaves, and derived categories of sheaves of modules [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq\Lambda$ be a finitely generated ideal, and put $P_n=\Lambda/I^n$ for integers $n\geq1$, with powers and quotient rings as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume $\Lambda/I$ is torsion as an additive group (each element is killed by a positive integer), and every $P_n$, placed in degree zero, is perfect over $\Lambda$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ define its reduction by derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]:
$$K_n:=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(P_n)_X\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},P_n).$$
Here $(P_n)_X$ and $\Lambda_X$ are constant sheaves of rings, and the underlying $\Lambda_X$-object is the derived tensor of [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Regard all reductions also in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $b\geq a\geq1$, define $q_{b,a}:K_b\to K_a$ there using the quotient map $P_b\to P_a$. The transition identities are $q_{a,a}=1$ and $q_{c,a}=q_{b,a}\circ q_{c,b}$ for $c\geq b\geq a$. The canonical normalization isomorphisms are
$$\theta_{b,a}:K_b\otimes^L_{(P_b)_X}(P_a)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a.$$
They are the scalar-extension associativity maps. For $c\geq b\geq a$, the composite of $\theta_{c,b}\otimes^L_{(P_b)_X}(P_a)_X$ with $\theta_{b,a}$ equals $\theta_{c,a}$ after the canonical associativity identification of the source; for $b=a$ normalization is the unit identification.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat representative Q of K with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and compose the localization of its quasi-isomorphic augmentation with the representative isomorphism. Define each reduction by localizing the termwise change of rings [def-pur-change-of-rings-complex] on the constant ring sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. No boundedness or flatness of a quotient over the original ring is needed.

Construct scalar-extension transposition and its inverse directly from sectionwise extension/restriction adjunctions and module sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Comparing restriction along the composite with successive restrictions [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] gives the balancing map by two lifts. On local generators it sends s tensor (r tensor m) to (s times psi(r)) tensor m. Lift the composite of the two scalar-extension units to construct the inverse, sending s tensor m to s times (1 tensor (1 tensor m)). Transposition reduces both inverse identities to evaluation on m; the formulas and preservation of one give identity. These maps commute with differentials and chain maps by the same generator formulas, giving the balancing chain isomorphism and its naturality. The changed complexes remain K-flat with flat terms by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], as required to compute successive derived extensions.

proof.text: The quotient maps of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] compose and are identities at equal indices. Use the scalar-extension unit, the identity-on-sections comparison for composing restrictions [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and the balancing map of step 2 to construct the transition chain map. Its local formula is r tensor m maps to pi(r) tensor m. The sheafification adjunction and tensor generation [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] prove uniqueness. Both differential compatibility and naturality follow by applying the original differential or chain map to m in this formula. The quotient identities prove the chain-map identities, which localization preserves.

proof.text: For c at least b at least a, transpose the proposed chain-map equality along the last two scalar extensions. Tensor generation [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] then reduces it to s tensor (r tensor (t tensor m)) with the transposed scalar factors equal to one. Apply the explicit balancing formulas and the functoriality of the constant quotient maps: the coefficient paths agree because quotient homomorphisms compose. Localize this equality to obtain the normalization cocycle. For the identity ring map, lift the identity-on-sections restriction isomorphism to obtain the unit map; its inverse is the scalar-extension unit. The two inverse identities follow after transposition. Its generator formula is s tensor m maps to s times m. This formula and the equal-index quotient identity identify normalization with the unit map before and after localization.

Specialize [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation] to the unit module over the quotient ring sheaf. The left unitor identifies restricted scalar extension with the tensor of the restricted quotient unit and the original module. Braid the factors to put the model first. Naturality of cancellation, the unitor and the braiding gives an isomorphism of termwise complexes. The single-complex tensor isomorphism identifies this termwise tensor with total tensor against the quotient module in degree zero. Localization yields exactly the object called derivedTensorRing in [def-weil-derived-tensor], hence the required reduction comparison. No quotient-flatness assumption is used.
